changes.after: Use when to choose one result from several possibilities.

before: A when expression chooses a branch result. The chosen result can initialize a variable.
For arbitrary integer choices, else covers values not named by earlier branches. Later sealed and enum types permit other exhaustive forms.
After one branch result is selected, later branches do not execute automatically as in a fallthrough-style switch.
Matching chooses a result; it does not assign a new value to the subject.
Expected output or behavior: read. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Test named and unmatched choices. Explain why only one branch supplies the result. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An expression is code that produces a value. A `when` expression chooses a path and uses that path's result.
Each branch names a match before `->` and a result after it. Kotlin checks the branches in order and uses the first match.
The `else` branch handles values that matched none of the earlier branches. It makes this integer choice complete: every possible input has a result.
Only the selected branch supplies the result. Reading choice does not change choice. The result goes into the separate name `label`.
The screen shows `read`. The value 1 matches the first branch, so label gets its text.
If choice matches neither 1 nor 2, the else branch supplies `help`. Kotlin does not continue through the other branches after choosing one.
